title: Refit a mini-split's two washed air filters
instruction: Put the two clean air filters back into the air conditioner, one in each bay, then take your hands away.
context: The mesh air filters of a wall-mounted ductless mini-split are cleaned every few weeks: the filters are taken out, washed, dried and refitted. In apartments, hotels and offices this is routine preventive maintenance. O*NET lists "Perform routine maintenance, such as ... replacing filters, or doing other preventive maintenance actions" as a task of general maintenance and repair workers (49-9071.00, 1,621,800 workers, BLS 2025). Refitting a filter is the fiddly part. Its top edge has to go up into a pocket behind a lip that hides it. Then the filter is swung upright while it is lifted, so its bottom edge passes over the two lugs at the bottom of the bay, and then it drops behind the lugs onto the ledge. A filter left on the lugs or out of its pocket bows away from the coil and lets dust past it.
setup: Two arms in front of a wall (bases 61 cm apart), seen by one overhead camera and a camera on each wrist. Distances are measured forward from the line between the arm bases and sideways from the midpoint between them; heights are above the table. (1) A white wall-mounted mini-split indoor unit, 82 x 26.5 x 24 cm, on the wall, centred, its front 38.5 cm forward and its underside 14 cm up. Its front panel has been lifted off its hinges for cleaning and set aside, so its filter bay is open. The bay holds two filters side by side, centred 18 cm left and right of the centre line, in front of the dark coil grille. Each filter's seat is a ledge 18 cm up. In front of each seat are two white lugs, 5 mm tall and 2 cm wide, 12 cm either side of the bay's centre. Along the bay's top is a 3 cm white lip, 35 to 38 cm up, with a 7 mm deep pocket behind it. A seated filter's top edge stands 1 cm up into the pocket, and the filter can be lifted 16 mm. A white rib separates the bays. (2) Two clean air filters, each 33.5 x 18 cm: a grey plastic frame 5 mm thick with 8 to 10 mm rails and a centre cross, grey mesh, 45 g. A pull tab, 2.4 cm wide, 3 cm long and 3 mm thick, sticks out from the middle of its bottom edge on the room side. They lie face up on the table, centred 18 cm left and right of the centre line, their bottom edges 12 cm forward, so each tab stands up at the edge nearer the arms. The layout is the same in every trial, as in the screenshot.
scoring: 1.0 as soon as all of these hold, with both filters still, for 1 s: both filters seated, each in its own bay; and each gripper's fingertip centre at least 3 cm in front of the unit. Seated means on the ledge behind both of its bottom lugs, with its top edge in the pocket behind the lip: its bottom edge within 2.5 mm of the seat front to back and 3 mm in height, upright within 3 degrees, and centred in its bay within 10 mm. Otherwise, judged at the end of the run: 0.75: both seated, but a gripper closer to the unit; 0.5: one filter seated; 0.25: no filter seated, but a filter's top edge is in its pocket behind the lip; 0.0: anything else. In a real trial a seated filter is checked by eye: its bottom edge sits behind both lugs, it is upright, and it does not come out when its tab is pulled straight out.
reset_notes: Nothing is consumed. For each filter: lift it 1.5 cm by its tab so that its bottom edge clears the lugs, pull the bottom out, lower the filter out of the pocket, and lay it face up on the table as in the screenshot.
fidelity: Rigid-body simulation (Isaac Sim 6.1 with PhysX, 20 Hz control) of a calibrated two-arm rig. Simplified: the unit hangs at bench height (real units are about 2 m up a wall) and only its front is modelled (the coil grille, the pockets, ledges and lugs); the filters are rigid frames whose mesh has no collision; dust and washing are not simulated; parts are boxes, and the cameras render at 320 x 176.
